purpose: Teacher-facing preview activities for the virtual classroom demo. These are safe teaching lenses, not claims about the official unit order or exact lesson titles.
virtual_only_notice: All listed flows describe actions inside this software. They are not real-world laboratory procedures.

grade_previews.title: Observing matter with a classroom solution
grade_previews.focus: Distinguish a solid, a liquid and a simple solution using the virtual model.
learning_goals: Identify a solid sample and a liquid sample.
Recognize that a uniform solution is a mixture.
virtual_flow: Open the Classroom Demo setup.
Select the beaker and read its Inspector panel.
Compare a solid sample with a liquid sample in the Library.
Observe the dissolution demo and describe what changed.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask students what they can see, what changed and what stayed the same.

grade_previews.title: Solutions, insoluble mixtures and separation ideas
grade_previews.focus: Compare a solution with an insoluble mixture and discuss how separation ideas differ.
learning_goals: Identify the solvent and solute in a classroom model.
Explain why some materials dissolve and others do not.
virtual_flow: Open the Classroom Demo setup.
Inspect the water and salt entries in the Learning Guide.
Compare the solution model with an insoluble reference material.
Discuss which mixture features are visible and which are only conceptual.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask which material acts as the solvent and how the model represents particles becoming distributed.

grade_previews.title: Saturation and closed-system reasoning
grade_previews.focus: Introduce the idea of a solubility limit and the use of a closed-system model.
learning_goals: Define a saturated solution at a conceptual level.
Distinguish dissolved material from visible undissolved solid.
Discuss why a simulation needs stated assumptions and limits.
virtual_flow: Open the Classroom Demo setup.
Read the Learning Guide section on saturation.
Use the Inspector to identify the contents and observations.
Discuss which aspects are simplified and which are represented by the software.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask students why a model must state its temperature and solubility assumptions before making quantitative claims.

grade_previews.title: Integrated Science: matter, energy and life systems
grade_previews.focus: Connect the classroom chemistry model to biology and Earth-system ideas.
learning_goals: Relate glucose and starch to biological energy ideas.
Describe photosynthesis and cellular respiration at a high level.
Explain why air and carbon dioxide matter in science beyond chemistry.
virtual_flow: Open the Classroom Demo setup.
Inspect a solution and review the explanation in the Learning Guide.
Compare glucose, starch and carbon dioxide as reference concepts.
Discuss how the virtual model links chemistry, biology and Earth science.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask students to connect an observable change with a possible explanation at the particle level.

grade_previews.title: Scientific models and pathway confirmation
grade_previews.focus: Evaluate model limits and confirm the student’s official Senior 2 pathway before planning lessons.
learning_goals: Separate a model's output from a measured result.
Explain why the exact Senior 2 pathway is required before official Chemistry mapping.
virtual_flow: Open the Classroom Demo setup.
Review one observation and its explanation in the Inspector.
Read the data-quality notes and curriculum status.
Compare the preview with the student's selected official pathway before using it for lesson planning.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask students which statements are direct observations, which are explanations and which are assumptions in the model.
